agent_report.discovery: Explored wp-admin and found need for content awareness - AI agents need to know what posts exist before helping with content management
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns post metadata including title, status, author, dates, excerpt, and comment count. Works for all authenticated users with edit_posts capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/get-post - Get full content of a specific post
garden-abilities/list-comments - List recent comments
garden-abilities/list-media - List media library items
garden-abilities/woo-store-status - Check WooCommerce setup
garden-abilities/create-draft - Create new draft posts
lessons_learned: Input schemas with no required params need 'default': {} to work via GET
Chat widget uses closed Shadow DOM - test via REST API first
Use existing categories (site, user) or register custom ones first

agent_report.discovery: Explored Site Health page (Tools → Site Health) and found valuable diagnostic data hidden multiple clicks deep. Critical issues, security concerns, and performance recommendations are exactly what AI agents need for proactive monitoring.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns overall_status (good/should_be_improved/critical), summary counts, critical_issues array, recommendations array, and passed_tests array. Requires view_site_health_checks capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/site-health-info - Return debug info tab data (PHP version, database info, etc.)
garden-abilities/plugin-status - Check for plugin updates and security issues
garden-abilities/theme-status - Analyze active and inactive themes
garden-abilities/error-log - Read recent PHP errors from debug.log
garden-abilities/cron-status - Check WordPress scheduled tasks
lessons_learned: Admin-only functions like get_core_updates() need manual require_once when running via REST
Some Site Health tests make slow HTTP requests - skip them for faster response
Wrap test execution in try/catch for graceful degradation
The Site Health API is powerful but underutilized - great opportunity for AI tools

agent_report.discovery: Explored WooCommerce Status page (WooCommerce → Status) and found comprehensive diagnostic data hidden 3+ clicks deep. Environment details, server capabilities, database health, theme compatibility, and store settings - exactly what AI agents need for troubleshooting e-commerce issues.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns overall_status (good/needs_attention/critical), detected issues with actionable hints, environment info (WooCommerce 10.3.5, WordPress 6.9-RC3, PHP 8.2.29), database size, theme compatibility, and store settings. Requires manage_woocommerce capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/woo-orders-summary - Get recent order statistics and status breakdown
garden-abilities/woo-products-status - Check product inventory levels and stock warnings
garden-abilities/woo-payment-gateways - List configured payment methods and their status
garden-abilities/woo-shipping-zones - Show shipping configuration and methods
garden-abilities/plugin-updates - Check for available plugin updates across the site
lessons_learned: Leverage existing APIs - WooCommerce's WC_REST_System_Status_V2_Controller already does the heavy lifting
Add intelligence, not just data - analyze and surface actionable issues rather than raw data dumps
Match existing permission models - use manage_woocommerce to follow WooCommerce's own access patterns
Return structured status levels (good/needs_attention/critical) so AI agents can quickly assess severity

agent_report.discovery: Explored WooCommerce Analytics dashboard and found critical business metrics (orders, sales, trends) buried multiple clicks deep. Store owners constantly ask 'How is my store doing?' - this ability answers that instantly.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns order counts by status, actionable orders count (pending+processing+on-hold), 7-day period metrics (total sales, items sold, average order value), and 5 most recent orders with customer details. Requires view_woocommerce_reports capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/woo-products-status - Low stock alerts, out-of-stock products, product performance
garden-abilities/woo-customer-insights - New vs returning customers, top customers, lifetime value
garden-abilities/woo-refunds-summary - Refund trends, reasons, and impact on revenue
garden-abilities/woo-revenue-trends - Week-over-week, month-over-month comparisons
lessons_learned: Use native WooCommerce APIs (wc_get_orders, wc_orders_count) rather than raw queries for HPOS compatibility
Add actionable intelligence - the 'actionable_count' field surfaces what matters most
Provide context with data - include date ranges so AI agents understand the timeframe
Match existing permissions - use view_woocommerce_reports to follow WooCommerce's access patterns

agent_report.discovery: Explored Tools → Scheduled Actions page and found Action Scheduler data buried 3+ clicks deep. This shows all background jobs managed by WooCommerce: pending tasks, completed actions, failed executions. Critical for diagnosing cron issues and monitoring background processing.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns overall_status (good/needs_attention), summary counts (pending, running, complete, failed, canceled), action groups with pending counts, next 10 pending actions with recurrence info, last 10 failed actions, and last 5 completed actions. Requires manage_options capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/scheduled-action-logs - Get detailed execution logs for a specific action
garden-abilities/run-scheduled-action - Manually trigger a pending action (write ability)
garden-abilities/scheduled-action-cleanup - Clear old completed actions to reduce database bloat
garden-abilities/cron-health - Check if WP-Cron is running properly by comparing scheduled vs actual execution times
lessons_learned: Action Scheduler loads lazily - not available in wp shell, only in full WordPress context (like REST API calls)
Schema validation is strict - if a field might be null, either omit it or declare it as nullable in the schema
Add intelligence, not just data - the 'issues' array with detected problems is more valuable than raw counts
Detect stuck actions - jobs pending for more than 1 hour often indicate cron issues

agent_report.discovery: Explored Dashboard → Updates page and found valuable update information buried there: WordPress core version, plugin updates, theme updates, and auto-update settings. Session 2 had previously suggested this as an idea for proactive security monitoring.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns overall_status (good/needs_attention/critical), summary counts (total plugins, active, updates available, auto-updates enabled), WordPress core info with update type classification (major/minor/security), plugin and theme update lists, and detected issues. Requires update_plugins capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/enable-auto-updates - Write ability to enable auto-updates for specific plugins
garden-abilities/update-plugin - Write ability to actually perform plugin updates
garden-abilities/plugin-changelog - Fetch changelog for a plugin's pending update
garden-abilities/plugin-security-scan - Check plugins against known vulnerability databases
garden-abilities/media-library-summary - List and search media library items
lessons_learned: Force update refresh with wp_update_plugins() and wp_update_themes() to ensure fresh data
Add intelligence, not just data - the issues array with severity levels is more valuable than raw counts
Follow WordPress permission patterns - use update_plugins capability for consistency
Include timestamps (checked_at) so AI agents understand data freshness

agent_report.discovery: Explored Media → Library page and found rich metadata scattered across individual media items. File names, MIME types, dimensions, alt text, URLs - exactly what AI agents need for content creation workflows. Session 6 had previously suggested this ability.
agent_report.testing_results: Successfully tested via REST API. Returns summary (total items, counts by type, storage estimate, alt text statistics), recent_items (10 most recent uploads with full metadata), and issues (accessibility warnings for missing alt text). Found 2 images with 100% missing alt text. Requires upload_files capability.
ideas: garden-abilities/search-media - Search media by filename, title, or caption
garden-abilities/update-alt-text - Write ability to add/update alt text on images
garden-abilities/unused-media - Find media items not attached to any content
garden-abilities/woo-products-status - Low stock alerts and inventory monitoring
garden-abilities/comments-summary - Overview of recent comments and moderation queue
lessons_learned: Sample-based estimates work - checking file sizes of recent 100 files provides good storage estimates without scanning entire uploads directory
Group data intelligently - grouping MIME types by category (image/video/audio) is more actionable than listing every specific type
Surface accessibility issues - missing alt text is common and AI agents can help address it
Include URLs - direct URLs to media files let AI agents reference them in generated content
